meetings.title: Special City Council
meetings.summary: The Jackson City Council held a special meeting on September 25, 2026, to handle year-end budget adjustments and several agreements. The council approved a $29,966,223 interdepartmental transfer to close out the FY2026 municipal budget, with funds moved from personnel services in police and public works and other categories to cover insurance, JTRAN, and other needs. The council also approved a $1,947,008 appropriation to the Jackson/Hinds Library System and accepted the Jackson Airport Authority budget for FY2026-2027. Additionally, the council authorized the mayor to execute a torch relay agreement with the Los Angeles Organizing Committee for the 2028 Olympics, making Jackson a host community, and approved a memorandum of agreement with the DEA for participation in a state and local law enforcement task force. All items passed 4-0.

topics.title: FY2026 Budget Revision
topics.note: Approved a $29,966,223 interdepartmental transfer to make final amendments to the FY2026 municipal budget, moving funds from various departments to cover shortfalls and close out the fiscal year.

topics.title: Police Department Personnel Savings
topics.note: The budget revision included transferring $2,220,648 from police department personnel services due to unfilled positions, which Councilman Foote noted means fewer officers on the street.

topics.title: Public Works Personnel Savings
topics.note: The budget revision included transferring $3,200,000 from public works personnel services due to unfilled positions, impacting road and drainage services.

topics.title: Operating Transfers to Outside Funds
topics.note: The budget revision included $3,700,000 in operating transfers from general government, representing money set aside for outside funds that was no longer needed.

topics.title: Landfill Sanitation Equipment
topics.note: The budget revision included $400,000 for landfill sanitation to purchase a dozer critical for getting the landfill fully online and complying with MDEQ regulations.

topics.title: Employee Group Insurance Fund
topics.note: The budget revision included $4,000,000 transferred into the employee group insurance fund because insurance costs were higher than expected.

topics.title: Franchise Cable Television Revenue Shortfall
topics.note: The budget revision decreased franchise cable television revenue by $500,000 due to lower-than-expected collections as more people stream instead of using cable.

topics.title: JTRAN Operating Transfers
topics.note: The budget revision included $4,000,000 in operating transfers to planning and development for balancing JTRAN, related to new buses.

topics.title: Audit Update
topics.note: CFO Jillian Caldwell reported that the city virtually met with auditors and is working to provide remaining items by next week, with the audit review to take a couple more weeks.

topics.title: Monthly Finance Committee Meetings
topics.note: Councilman Parkinson noted that the council has committed to monthly finance committee meetings starting after October actuals to monitor the budget throughout the year.

topics.title: Jackson/Hinds Library System Appropriation
topics.note: Approved an appropriation of $1,947,008 to the Jackson/Hinds Library System for fiscal year 2026-2027.

topics.title: Jackson Airport Authority Budget
topics.note: Accepted the budget of the Jackson Airport Authority for fiscal year 2026-2027.

topics.title: Olympic Torch Relay Agreement
topics.note: Authorized the mayor to execute a torch relay agreement with the Los Angeles Organizing Committee for the 2028 Olympics, making Jackson a host community and establishing a community task force.

topics.title: DEA Task Force Memorandum
topics.note: Authorized the mayor to enter into a memorandum of agreement with the U.S. Department of Justice, Drug Enforcement Administration, for participation in the DEA state and local law enforcement task force.

meetings.title: City Council
meetings.summary: The Jackson City Council approved a claims docket of $3.74 million, including $996,580 for street resurfacing and $965,638 for traffic signal work, and confirmed three mayoral appointments to the Planning Board. The council authorized a debt-collection agreement with Municipal Intercept Company to recover unpaid fines and fees through state tax intercepts, and approved a $560,747.50 correction to the Shaw Road Bridge contract despite one no vote over contractor delays. The council also discussed street resurfacing plans, Entergy lighting concerns, and Tennis Center South management, and heard public comments on a censure petition against Councilman Stokes, flooding, and housing conditions. A proclamation declared September Service Dog Month, and the council entered closed session for litigation with no action taken.

topics.title: Public comment: censure petition against Councilman Stokes
topics.note: Norma Michael presented a petition signed by 90 citizens demanding formal censure, public reprimand, committee review, and a $500 penalty for Stokes over derogatory remarks at the Sept. 8 meeting.

topics.title: Public comment: street flooding and paving
topics.note: Diane Roby described five years of flooding on her street, saying the street is unlevel and needs paving; constituent services took her information.

topics.title: Public comment: housing and code enforcement
topics.note: Ricky Banks criticized the city's handling of dilapidated houses and unhoused residents, urging a study to help families repair homes.

topics.title: Public comment: Dale Haven Manor conditions
topics.note: Bobby Coleman described crime and poor conditions at a senior disability apartment complex and thanked officials for weekend water delivery.

topics.title: Public comment: St. Andrews Drive repaving
topics.note: Charles Johnson urged prioritizing repaving of St. Andrews Drive west of Old Canton Road, noting it has not been repaved in over 40 years.

topics.title: Public comment: street resurfacing and state match
topics.note: Virgil Payne said Hinds County has about $96,000 in leftover state allocation that could save the city 30% if used immediately for street work.

topics.title: Public comment: tax sale property issues
topics.note: Victoria Jacob Branson raised concerns about tax sale property transfers and asked the city to help homeowners avoid losing property.

topics.title: Public comment: neighborhood blight on Eminence and Newman
topics.note: Loretha Wales said two streets in Ward 3 look like a wasteland and that reported property owners have not cleaned up dumping.

topics.title: Council president apology for decorum incident
topics.note: Council President Hartley apologized for a prior meeting incident and said steps will be taken to prevent similar behavior.

topics.title: Consent agenda approved
topics.note: The consent agenda was approved 6-0 by one motion without separate discussion.

topics.title: Solid waste disposal fee ordinance introduced
topics.note: An ordinance amending solid waste facility disposal fees was introduced.

topics.title: Claims docket approved
topics.note: The council approved a claims docket of $3,741,384.90; largest claims included $996,580.16 for street resurfacing and $965,638.20 for traffic signals.

topics.title: Payroll approved
topics.note: The council approved the gross payroll and deduction claims by a 7-0 vote.

topics.title: Payment for 2525 Robinson Street
topics.note: The council approved September 2026 payment for the property at 2525 Robinson Street, a heavily used library, by a 5-0-1 vote.

topics.title: Planning Board appointment: Vanessa Gray
topics.note: The council confirmed Vanessa Gray to the Planning Board representing Ward 4.

topics.title: Planning Board appointment: Hosea Hines
topics.note: The council confirmed Hosea Hines to the Planning Board representing Ward 6.

topics.title: Planning Board appointment: James Shoulders
topics.note: The council confirmed James Shoulders to the Planning Board representing Ward 4.

topics.title: Landscaping contract with MS Yard Barber
topics.note: The council approved a contract with MS Yard Barber LLC for landscaping and ground maintenance, funded by a federal grant that requires a contractor.

topics.title: MetLife insurance renewal
topics.note: The council approved a policy renewal with MetLife for group life and AD&D insurance for 2027 by a 5-1-1 vote.

topics.title: 3P Benefits Solutions cafeteria plan
topics.note: The council approved an administrative services agreement with 3P Benefits Solutions for a Section 125 cafeteria plan by a 5-1-1 vote.

topics.title: Surplus property conveyance to Wil-Mat Investments
topics.note: The council approved conveying parcels 70-79, 110-24, and 110-25 to Wil-Mat Investments for residential development by a 6-0-1 vote.

topics.title: Entergy power line raise for traffic signal project
topics.note: The council approved payment to Entergy Mississippi to raise a power line for the Traffic Signal Group B project by a 7-0 vote after discussion of citywide lighting issues.

topics.title: Shaw Road Bridge contract correction
topics.note: The council approved amending the Hemphill Construction contract to $560,747.50 by a 6-1 vote; Stokes voted no over contractor delays.

topics.title: Municipal Intercept Company debt collection
topics.note: The council approved a resolution supporting an agreement with Municipal Intercept Company to collect unpaid debts through state tax intercepts by a 5-1-1 vote.

topics.title: Service Dog Month proclamation
topics.note: Mayor Horhn proclaimed September as Service Dog Month and presented the proclamation to Melanie Courtney and her service dog Navi.

topics.title: Office of Publication relocation discussion
topics.note: CAO Peter Davidson asked that the Office of Publication relocation be referred to committee after a building fire; the item was referred to planning committee.

topics.title: Neighborhood street resurfacing discussion
topics.note: Councilman Foote urged continuing the existing unit-cost paving contract without delay; the mayor said over 600 streets are being resurfaced and a $40 million bond package is moving forward.

topics.title: Mary Jones Community Center discussion
topics.note: Councilman Stokes raised the poor condition of the center and a family thanked police for progress in the Tayshia Fortune case; ownership and repurposing were discussed.

topics.title: Private police and armed group discussion
topics.note: Stokes raised concerns about armed groups walking through neighborhoods; Chief Brackney said open carry is legal and police coordinated with intelligence agencies.

topics.title: City workforce utilization and accountability
topics.note: Councilman Hartley asked for metrics linking spending to services; CAO Davidson said KPIs have been sent to departments and data will start monthly review in late October.

topics.title: Tennis Center South discussion
topics.note: Residents and tennis players asked for qualified management at Battlefield Park and Tennis Center South; officials said funding exists to hire a tennis pro and lighting for Battlefield is identified.

topics.title: Closed session for litigation
topics.note: The council entered closed session to discuss litigation; afterward the president said no official action was taken.

meetings.title: Zoning Meeting
meetings.summary: The Jackson City Council zoning meeting tabled two cases (4332 and 4339) until October 19, 2026, because the zoning division failed to notify all parties, including opponents, and the council wanted everyone present. The council approved a conditional use permit for Terranee Brent to operate a community recreational center with skating, arcade games, fitness training, and events at 540 Raymond Road, Suite B, for one year. It also approved a five-foot front-yard setback variance for Annie Lewis to continue building an open carport at 1021 Westway Street. The council then approved renewal of special exceptions and use permits for one year. No dollar figures were discussed.

topics.title: Call to order and introductions
topics.note: Meeting called to order at 2:32 PM; no introductions were made.

topics.title: Tabling of cases 4332 and 4339
topics.note: Zoning requested moving both cases to October because all parties, including opponents, were not notified; council agreed to table until October 19.

topics.title: Public comment on tabling
topics.note: Terrace Harris, an applicant, expressed frustration over delays and asked for a prompt hearing; council said the case would be heard in October.

topics.title: Legal explanation of notice failure
topics.note: Deputy City Attorney Carrie Johnson explained the case was first tabled in November 2025 and that only interested parties, not opponents, had been noticed.

topics.title: Clerk clarifies notice responsibility
topics.note: Shaniqui, clerk of council, said zoning normally handles notices and that the council only noticed its own meeting.

topics.title: Zoning acknowledges misunderstanding
topics.note: Zoning administrator acknowledged a misunderstanding about notifying parties and said notices would be sent that day.

topics.title: Councilman Stokes comments on delays
topics.note: Stokes said he thought the opposing party wanted to move forward and mentioned a letter from opponents; he expressed frustration that the case could not be heard.

topics.title: Agreement to hear cases in October
topics.note: After discussion, council agreed to hear both cases at the October 19 meeting; legal and zoning concurred.

topics.title: Case 4332 tabling details
topics.note: Carrie Johnson noted case 4332 was tabled at the applicant's request, not by a council member.

topics.title: Councilman's apology and update
topics.note: A councilman apologized for missing a prior meeting due to a death in the family and said he would be ready to move forward in October.

topics.title: Case 4339 conditional use permit
topics.note: Council considered a conditional use permit for Terranee Brent to operate a community recreational center at 540 Raymond Road, Suite B.

topics.title: Legal explanation of conditional use
topics.note: Deputy City Attorney explained the permit is needed because the uses are not allowed by right and would be limited to the applicant and time period.

topics.title: Council discussion on permit terms
topics.note: Councilman Stokes confirmed the permit is for one year and only for the specific applicant; the applicant was present.

topics.title: Neighborhood leader's input
topics.note: Councilman said the neighborhood leader initially opposed due to past history but agreed to a one-year trial after receiving more information.

topics.title: Vote on case 4339
topics.note: The conditional use permit for Terranee Brent was approved by a vote of 5-1.

topics.title: Case 4340 variance request
topics.note: Petition for a variance of up to five feet from the required 25-foot front setback at 1021 Westway Street for an open carport; applicant Annie Lewis represented by Joby Austin.

topics.title: Council comments on case 4340
topics.note: Councilwoman Clay expressed support and said the neighborhood had no opposition; President Hartley emphasized following law and ordinance.

topics.title: Staff presentation on variance
topics.note: Zoning staff presented photos and maps, noted surrounding R1A single-family zoning, and recommended approval based on ordinance criteria.

topics.title: Vote on case 4340
topics.note: The variance for Annie Lewis was approved by a vote of 5-0.

topics.title: Special exception and use permit renewals
topics.note: Council approved renewal of special exceptions and use permits for one year by a vote of 4-0.

topics.title: Adjournment
topics.note: Meeting adjourned with no further business.

Variance of up to five feet from front setback for Annie Lewis at 1021 Westway Street (case 4340)

meetings.body: Jackson City Council Public Safety & Parks Committee
meetings.title: Public Safety & Parks Committee Meeting
meetings.summary: The Jackson City Council Public Safety and Parks Committee discussed police officer retention and recruitment with Chief Rochelle Brackney, who reported the department has about 208 sworn officers, with roughly 130 in patrol. She said an October academy class could bring in at least 33 recruits across agencies, with five already cleared and six more in testing. Brackney outlined recruitment and retention efforts including loan forgiveness, sign-on bonuses, specialty assignments, a health and wellness initiative, and a possible sergeant examination. The committee also discussed the Real-Time Command Center and camera system, with Brackney reporting many cameras are inoperable and that the center is understaffed. The committee agreed to pursue AI software and further review camera contracts, possibly in executive session.

topics.title: Officer retention and recruitment
topics.note: Chief Brackney reported about 208 sworn officers, with an October academy class expecting at least 33 recruits across agencies.

topics.title: Academy class and recruitment pipeline
topics.note: Five recruits cleared paperwork, six passed physical fitness, and seven are testing; Alcorn State pipeline discussed.

topics.title: Recruitment incentives
topics.note: Brackney proposed loan forgiveness, sign-on bonuses, and specialty assignments to attract and retain officers.

topics.title: Health and wellness initiative
topics.note: Proposal to HR for a phased wellness program for police, fire, and public works, intended to be cost-neutral.

topics.title: Drone program
topics.note: City awarded a grant to purchase two unmanned aerial devices; officers could train as pilots.

topics.title: Entry-level qualifications
topics.note: Minimum requirements include high school education or GED, age 21 with waivers possible, physical fitness, background and psychological tests.

topics.title: Civilian pathways in JPD
topics.note: Brackney listed non-uniform roles such as animal control, criminalist, 911 operator, and detention officer.

topics.title: Sworn officer count and resignations
topics.note: Sworn officers down to about 208 from 212; recent resignations included officers under investigation.

topics.title: Reasons for resignations
topics.note: Brackney cited neglect of duty, incomplete reports, body camera issues, and possible criminal referrals to the DA.

topics.title: Training and policy compliance
topics.note: Discussion on need for upscaling, lesson plans, and verifying officers understand policies.

topics.title: Termination procedures and HR coordination
topics.note: Brackney said she works with HR and legal on standardized termination and performance improvement plans.

topics.title: Performance evaluations
topics.note: Uncertainty about quarterly evaluations; Brackney asked supervisors to keep electronic folders on officers.

topics.title: Sergeant examination
topics.note: Council approved an outside formal sergeant examination through civil service; no testing since 2020-2021.

topics.title: Quality vs. quantity in hiring
topics.note: Brackney said she will not hire desperately and prefers 200 quality officers over 275 with integrity issues.

topics.title: Patrol staffing levels
topics.note: About 130 patrol officers across four precincts and three shifts, averaging roughly 11 per precinct per shift.

topics.title: Take-home vehicle policy
topics.note: Brackney clarified no new policy; city policy requires 24-hour employees and Hinds County residency unless approved.

topics.title: Real-Time Command Center staffing
topics.note: Center should be staffed by civilians; currently down to two positions, with four allocated and interviews underway.

topics.title: Camera system status
topics.note: Reported 88 operable and 84 inoperable city asset cameras; 58 operable and 20 inoperable LPR cameras; many donor cameras inoperable.

topics.title: AI software for cameras
topics.note: Demonstration of AI integration to pull data from multiple systems and send alerts; council supportive of moving forward.

topics.title: Camera costs and contracts
topics.note: JPD pays about $88 monthly for energy and $43 for AT&T per camera; CAO and chief reviewing contracts and grant funding.

topics.title: Drones for streetlight mapping
topics.note: Brackney suggested using new drones to identify streetlights that are out and report to public works.

topics.title: Future metrics and KPIs
topics.note: Committee will ask departments for metrics and key performance indicators after budget hearings.

money: $4,500 per officer cost recouped from state for academy training
$1.4 million in overtime for JPD
$88 monthly energy cost per camera
$43 monthly AT&T connection cost per camera
$100 to $120 per camera monthly for some city-supported cameras

meetings.title: Finance
meetings.summary: The Jackson City Council Finance Committee met on July 15, 2026, to discuss the city's budget and revenue shortfall. The chair announced that the city is not operating with a deficit but is receiving less revenue than expected, and outlined cost-control measures including freezing overtime, capital outlays, travel, and new equipment. The CFO was directed to adjust the budget by removing unused line items and to report back with updated figures. Councilman Ashby Foote raised concerns about funds deposited with the new bank, JP Morgan Chase, and called for a review of contracts from the previous administration. The meeting was adjourned without any votes.

topics.title: Call to Order and Opening Remarks
topics.note: Chair Montyne Clay called the finance committee meeting to order at 10:04 AM.

topics.title: Budget Status and Revenue Shortfall
topics.note: Chair stated the city is not operating with a deficit but revenue is below expectations and expenditures are within receipts.

topics.title: Proposed Cost-Control Measures
topics.note: Suggestions include freezing non-essential overtime, capital outlays, travel, and new equipment, and limiting operating expenses.

topics.title: Budget Adjustment Directive to CFO
topics.note: CFO instructed to remove unused line items and reduce other professional services to actual spending, then report back.

topics.title: Accounting and Reconciliation Improvements
topics.note: Recommendation to reconcile bank statements monthly by the 15th and post data in real time.

topics.title: Three-Year Budget Trend Review
topics.note: Suggestion to review three years of financial data before making changes to the 2026-2027 budget.

topics.title: Spending Guidance to Departments
topics.note: Departments advised not to spend based on paper money and to avoid unnecessary spending in the last two months.

topics.title: No Deficit Declaration
topics.note: Chair reiterated that the city does not have a deficit in terms of expenditures.

topics.title: CAO Comments on Collaboration
topics.note: Chief Administrative Officer Pieter Teeuwissen thanked the chair and council for collaboration on budget matters.

topics.title: Adjournment Attempt
topics.note: Chair attempted to adjourn, but Councilman Foote indicated he had questions and comments.

topics.title: Update on Funds at JP Morgan Chase
topics.note: CFO Jillian Caldwell reported that 90% of city funds, approximately $90 million, are now at Chase, with some left at old banks for outstanding checks.

topics.title: Interest Earnings Report Request
topics.note: Foote requested a report on interest earned on new accounts; CFO agreed to prepare it.

topics.title: Review of Previous Administration Contracts
topics.note: Foote called for reviewing and potentially redoing contracts from the previous administration, citing missed revenue and past prosecutions.

topics.title: Parking Meter Contract Concerns
topics.note: Foote noted that the parking meter contract has generated no funds for the city despite promises.

topics.title: Payroll Spending vs. Budget Request
topics.note: Foote requested a comparison of payroll spending to budget for each department with two months left in the fiscal year.

topics.title: Chair's Response and Adjournment
topics.note: Chair stated numbers would not be discussed today, legal will review contracts, and adjourned the meeting.

money: $90 million in city funds on deposit at Chase bank
